title: Creator of free Adobe clones unveils open-source Microsoft Office Excel, PowerPoint, and Word replications — Autodesk tools and other subscription-based services may come next
source_used: Tom's Hardware (fulltext fetched by main session)
key_facts: Brandon Thomas, developer of ArtCraft (open-source creative tools meant to replicate Adobe applications for free), announced three apps to replace Microsoft Office tools: GridCraft (Excel), DeckCraft (PowerPoint) and WordCraft (Word).
The apps were created with Claude and shared on the ArtCraft GitHub page, free for anyone to download.
Tom's Hardware says it has since found that the Reddit user u/ai_art_is_art, behind the earlier Adobe-style tools, is Brandon Thomas, a software engineer with 15 years of experience.
After ArtCraft became popular, critics attacked 'vibecoded' software and 'AI slop'; Thomas answered on X with a post dated 9 Oct 2026 saying he does know how to code.
One of ArtCraft's selling points is running all its software on Windows, macOS and Linux with an identical experience.
Tom's Hardware says Microsoft, like Adobe, is widely criticised for moving from one-time purchases to subscriptions, and reads the project as partly a protest against that.
ArtCraft's Discord community is growing fast; a CAD tool (CADcraft) is often requested by 3D-printing and engineering users who dislike Autodesk.
Tom's Hardware says most of these apps are still far from what they intend to replace.
quote_evidence: Brandon Thomas, developer of ArtCraft, a suite of open-source creative tools meant to replicate Adobe applications for free, has now announced apps to replace Microsoft Office tools such as Excel, PowerPoint, and Word, respectively, named GridCraft, DeckCraft, and WordCraft, that are created with Claude.
Thomas has shared his new clones to ArtCraft GitHub, making them free for all to download.
Most of these apps are still far from what they intend to replace, however, so we'll have to see how deep this message cuts.
why_it_matters_hint: Free, open-source stand-ins for subscription office software are appearing quickly thanks to AI coding, but they are still far from the real programs.
event_date: Not stated for the new apps; Tom's Hardware published 11 Oct 2026; the developer's X post quoted in it is dated 9 Oct 2026.
notes: Follow-up of our 9 Oct 2026 edition (Tom's Hardware report on the Adobe-style tools by u/ai_art_is_art). New today: three Office-style apps, and the developer is now named. No outside testing of the apps is reported in this article.
